A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VolSplat, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. All nine pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2 were inspected. v1 contains no appendix; v2 includes Appendices A–D.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction results on RealEstate10K, ScanNet and ACID, together with voxel-size and decoder ablations in Tables I–V.

after.justification: v2 retains original reconstruction experiments and adds multi-view results, a residual-design ablation, efficiency measurements and qualitative comparisons, including in its appendices.

M1.justification: The specified Gaussian parameter vector changes from 18 to 38 dimensions. Equation (9) changes the center offset from r*sigmoid(offset) to r*(sigmoid(offset)-0.5), allowing movement on both sides of the voxel center. These locally revise the reported parameterization; the feature lifting, voxel aggregation, residual U-Net and training loss remain. The PDFs do not establish whether these revisions reflect implementation changes or documentation corrections.

E1.justification: Both versions train and evaluate on RealEstate10K and ScanNet and evaluate zero-shot transfer to ACID. The novel-view synthesis task and represented domains remain unchanged. Additional input-view counts vary settings within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds AnySplat and WorldMirror to the RealEstate10K and ScanNet comparisons. In the ACID comparison, GGN is added and pixelSplat is removed. These substantially extend comparator participation across the existing benchmarks; AnySplat was only discussed as related work in v1.

E3.justification: v1 reports six-view evaluation; v2 adds 12- and 24-view evaluations and explicitly uses 12 views for the ablations. Appendix B introduces a controlled six-view memory/runtime comparison on one H20 GPU. Table 1 also reports retrained baselines and supplies ground-truth poses to AnySplat and WorldMirror, while v1 explicitly allowed GGN extra input views.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained voxel-size and decoder studies, v2 adds a test removing residual prediction, input-view scalability analysis, and computational tradeoff analysis in Appendix B. Tables 4–5 add resource measurements, and Figure 7 supplements the existing Gaussian visualization with density maps. These materially broaden the evidence examining component necessity, spatial allocation and efficiency.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The expanded experiments continue to report point estimates.

E6.justification: RealEstate10K baseline values are revised in v2's reported retrained comparison: DepthSplat PSNR changes from 27.47 to 30.52, while VolSplat remains 31.30 at six views. New 12/24-view, comparator, efficiency and qualitative results are added; ablation values now refer to 12 views. Benchmark PGS entries are removed. New rankings are mixed: WorldMirror has lower LPIPS at 12/24 views, and MVSplat has higher SSIM at 24 views.

T1.justification: Equation (9) substantively revises the mathematical definition of the Gaussian center offset from a one-sided range to a symmetric range around the voxel center. The remaining mathematical formulation is largely retained, apart from notation refinements; neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central voxel-alignment contribution and reconstruction-quality claims remain. However, v1's introduction emphasizes convenient integration of auxiliary depth and point-cloud signals, whereas v2 claims its unified voxel space eliminates the need for such ad hoc priors or auxiliary supervision. This changes a stated benefit without replacing the main contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly identifies the static-scene assumption and explains dynamic-scene ghosting and blur. v2 also adds explanations for small-voxel degradation, the importance of residual refinement, and practical efficiency. Its discussion attributes AnySplat and WorldMirror's lower scores to their pose-free design and ineffective use of supplied poses. These substantially expand applicability qualifications and interpretations.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly documents 128 inverse-depth candidates, MinkowskiEngine, degree-2 spherical harmonics, gradient clipping, eight target views, view-sampling rules and ScanNet fine-tuning from a RealEstate10K checkpoint. These are disclosures, not established procedural changes. Reported training hardware changes from four A100s to four H20s. Code availability wording changes from already available online to supplementary code and a promised public release; actual access cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds a limited set of references, including WorldMirror, No Pose at All, fuse-and-refine, Minkowski convolutional networks and SSIM. The TranSplat citation changes from Kim et al.'s transparent-object manipulation paper to Zhang et al.'s generalizable reconstruction paper. The broader positioning against pixel-aligned and voxel-fusion approaches remains.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the abstract, rewrites several introductory paragraphs, standardizes headings and notation, and updates authors and affiliations. Appendices organize additional supporting material, but the main introduction–related work–method–experiments–conclusion narrative and much of its prose remain.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, with rearranged schematics and extensively revised displays. The combined qualitative comparison is split and expanded; ACID comparisons, density maps and three appendix image grids are added. Table 1 gains grouped view-count columns, ablation tables gain resource columns, and a separate efficiency table is introduced.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 provides more useful reproduction details, component tests, efficiency evidence and explicit failure conditions. These improve assessability. The gain is tempered by internal overstatement: Table 1 claims superiority on every metric and view setting despite WorldMirror's better 12/24-view LPIPS and MVSplat's better 24-view SSIM. Public code-release wording also becomes less definite. The net improvement is therefore limited.
